analysis.title: US Equities Mid-Day Color (GS Equities Mid-Day Color, 23 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Calmer but cautious session on 10/23 with muted volumes and NDX > SPX > RTY after the 10/22 de-grossing event. More than 70% of the SPX is in the red, a flip from the prior day's breadth.
Brent is above $117/bbl on increased Middle East tensions, which the desk says is not helping the equity backdrop.

Reversion is under way after 10/22's violent moves. Momentum (GSPRHIMO) is +2.4% after closing -8% on 10/22, which erased its YTD gains. The hedge fund VIP positioning pair (GSTHVIPP) is +38bps after closing -4.2% on 10/22, its worst move since 2011.
NDX is +30bps after its worst day since mid-June. The AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is +45bps after finishing -6% on 10/22, and is down 23% from its June highs.

Single-stock moves: TNGX -12.9% after Phase 1/2 data for Vopimetostath at EMSO, with 7-figure volume across multiple players. INFY -4.9% after cutting FY revenue guidance and citing softer volumes. BE -11.9% and FIX -7.8% after strong headline results.
Towers are higher after SPCX headlines about securing 80k cell sites: CCI +9.2%, SBAC +1.8%, AMT +2.6%.
Earnings next week: 44% of the S&P reports. GOOGL and MSFT report Wednesday 10/28 and AMZN Thursday 10/29, following META and AAPL this week. The Fed rate decision is also Wednesday 10/28.
Technicals: volume is -12% vs the 5-day moving average. ETFs are 34% of the tape, up 4% vs the 20-day average. Top of Book liquidity is -17% vs the 5-day average.
CTAs are sellers in all scenarios over the next week: $15bn in a flat tape, $2.3bn in an up tape and $20.6bn in a down tape, out of the US.

Desk flows: activity is 4 out of 10 and overall franchise flows are skewed 2% better for sale. Long-only clients are 4.5% better for sale, with supply in real estate, industrials and utilities. Hedge funds are 2.5% better for sale, with supply in consumer discretionary, consumer staples and energy.

Chart of the Day: 10/22 was the 5th largest de-grossing event of the year at -1.6 SD and was driven entirely by long selling, the largest since September 2025. 9 of 11 sectors saw unwinds. Info tech had long selling plus short additions, its largest net selling since September 2024.
